move: photos clip-wipe in from the right, slow push-in, captions roll
how: Three full-frame photos stack in a 900x560 frame. Each visible photo drifts scale 1.08->1.0 and xPercent 0->-1.5 linearly for its whole life; every 1s (33% of the 3s) the next photo wipes in from clip-path inset(0 0 0 100%) to inset(0) over 0.75s with expo.inOut while its scale settles 1.18->1.08, stacked above with zIndex. Captions roll out yPercent -110 (power2.in) and the new one rolls in from 110 (expo.out) with the text swapped by tl.call; the side thumbnail highlight and a serif counter follow each beat. The first photo wipes back on top at 92% so the last frame matches the first.
adapt: Replace the three background images, caption names and counter labels; add photos by extending the wipeIn/settle calls at 1s intervals. Keep the 0.75s expo.inOut wipe and the linear push-in.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the frame with N photo layers, thumbs and captions from shot.images; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with each wipe at (0.25 + k*0.333)*D. The tl.call text swaps and document.querySelector('.t1'/'.n') must be scoped to el; tl.set at time 0 resets zIndex and clipPath so seeking back works.
caveats: clip-path wipes on three full-frame cover images, fairly heavy per frame
caption text is swapped by tl.call so scrubbing backwards shows stale text until the reset call at 0.01
